article_limitations: Disposition aggregate_only: the source reports 22 patients with antisynthetase syndrome and interstitial lung disease only as a series (counts, percentages, mean age); no patient has individual identity evidence, so no individual patient records are created and series statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 22 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the 22 stated individuals can be enumerated.

Series counts are arithmetically consistent (10/22 = 45% triad and 12/22 = 55% ILD only; patterns 6 + 5 + 2 + 4 + 5 = 22; fibrotic 2 definite UIP + 1 probable UIP + 2 fibrotic NSIP = 5). The antisynthetase antibody list (anti-Jo-1 six, anti-OJ, anti-PL-12, anti-PL-7 and anti-EJ one each) accounts for 10 of the 22 patients diagnosed with ASS; the source does not state antisynthetase antibody results for the other 12, and no antibody is mapped to a patient. Not reconciled.

Source wording kept as printed, not corrected: anti-RF is glossed as anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies; antinuclear antibodies are abbreviated ANF; the study period is described as the last five years while records were reviewed from 2014 to 2020; the mediastinal window is printed as window level 400–500 HU and window width 20–40 HU.

Single-patient counts (erythema in only one patient; anti-OJ, anti-PL-12, anti-PL-7, anti-EJ, anti-SSB and anti-RF each in one patient; one patient with probable UIP) are series statistics; none is linked to an identifiable patient or to another statement about the same person, so they do not individuate a patient and the article stays aggregate_only.

The results text reports that pleural effusion was present in 9 patients (41%) and pulmonary hypertension in 6 (27%) without saying which patients; the rest of the series counts likewise cannot be assigned to individuals.

Fig. 1 to Fig. 9 each show one or more unidentified series members; the text does not link any image to a numbered patient, so ownership is unresolved and none is EHR-includable. Pixels were reviewed in the separate visual target.

Fig. 4 caption says the two images show the same patient at different levels; this links only its two panels to one unidentified series member (one of the 2 mixed NSIP/OP patients) and does not individuate a patient with any other stated fact. Whether the panels of Figs. 2 and 5 show the same patient is not stated.
Panel letters: the Fig. 1, 7 and 8 captions name panels (a) and (b); the Fig. 2, 4 and 5 captions name no panel letters, and their a/b labels are taken from the white letters printed on the images.

Fig. 9: the caption text states a main pulmonary arterial diameter of 38 mm with a pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio greater than 1:1 for the one unidentified patient shown; the image itself prints 32 mm and 38 mm beside two measurement lines. The printed values are pixel content (visual target only). The caption does not name the vessel measured by the 32 mm line, and with no patient record the caption value is not a patient fact.
The source has no supplements or tables; the only quantitative image text is the two printed measurement labels in Fig. 9, kept in the visual target as pixel content.
